title: Lawmakers write to ID verification companies after September IDScan breach
date_note: The Record (24 November) says the letter was sent on Monday, 23 November.
summary: The Record reports that six bipartisan US lawmakers sent a letter on Monday to several identity verification companies, including IDScan, asking how they manage customers' sensitive data and defend it against AI-enabled attacks. It follows a September breach of IDScan's cloud platform. The Record says the breach led to scans of more than 150 million people's drivers' licenses appearing for sale on the dark web.
plain: US lawmakers asked ID verification companies how they protect scanned IDs after a September breach at IDScan. The Record says scans of more than 150 million people's IDs were put up for sale.
exec: Lawmakers are pressing ID verification firms on data handling after a breach in which, The Record says, scans of more than 150 million people's drivers' licenses were offered for sale.
impact: The Record says IDScan did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

evidence.quote: a September breach that led to scans of more than 150 million people's drivers' licenses

validation.note: One publisher (The Record); the letter itself was not read.

review.note: Compared letter, 150 million figure, cloud and AI wording against The Record
